## The question this pass was run to answer

Session N+11's brief named this paper as one of two places a *barrier
remark* about the greedy/covering method for Δ-systems might live — the
published relative, if there is one, of `Profile.greedy_forces_erdos_rado`
("no argument bottoming out at the greedy cover step can beat Erdős–Rado
1960"). Rule 19 blocked reporting the negative while the paper was
located and unopened.

## The answer

**The paper contains no Δ-system material of any kind.** Not a remark,
not a lemma, not a citation. The words *Δ-system* and *sunflower* do not
occur on any of the 31 pages, `f(k,r)` in Kostochka's sense does not
occur, Erdős–Rado 1960 is not among the nine references, and neither is
Abbott. It is a paper about a different problem that shares the phrase
"intersecting family".

## What it is actually about

The Erdős–Rothschild–Szemerédi problem (p. 178, §1.1): how large can an
intersecting family `F` of `r`-subsets of an `n`-set be if **every point
has degree at most `c|F|`**? Write `f(n,r,c)` for the maximum. The paper
generalises the known cases to all `c` via a linear-programming quantity.

The machinery is fractional matchings and covers (`ν*`, `τ*`, LP
duality), `ν`-critical *nuclei*, Baranyai's factorisation theorem, and
Pelikán's theorem on sets meeting all lines of a projective plane. The
extremal families are built from projective planes `P_k`.

## The one thing in it that touches this development

p. 186, in the case `1/2 ≤ c < 2/3`: the extremal family is `F[H_1]`
where `H_1` is *"a 3-uniform, intersecting set system with 10 members on
a 6-element set"*, and *"There exists exactly one such `H_1`"*
(Figure 1, p. 187, is a dot diagram of it and of five relatives).

Those are exactly the parameters of `Intersecting.iota3`, the witness for
`ι(3) = 10`. **The identification is not made here** — Figure 1 is a
diagram this pass did not decode, and Füredi's uniqueness is inside his
own hypotheses. What *is* checked, in
`rust/tests/support.rs::the_iota_three_witness_is_also_ekr_extremal`, is
the parameter coincidence and the reason it is not a coincidence at all:
`10 = ½C(6,3)`, so a 10-member intersecting family of 3-sets on six
points is an **EKR-extremal** family at `n = 2r`, picking exactly one set
from each of the ten complementary pairs. The repository's witness does
that. So at `b = 3` the sunflower-free constraint costs **nothing**: the
largest intersecting sunflower-free family of 3-sets is as large as the
largest intersecting family of 3-sets on six points.

## Notation hazard — the third `f` in this corpus

| symbol | meaning | source |
|---|---|---|
| `f(n,k)` | least `N` forcing a `k`-sunflower in an `n`-uniform family | this development, `Sunflower.UpperBound` |
| `f(k,r)` | the **largest** `k`-uniform family with no `r`-Δ-system | [Kos00] p. 1 |
| `f(n,r,c)` | the largest **intersecting** `r`-uniform family on `n` points with max degree `≤ c\|F\|` | [Fur78] p. 178 |

Three different functions, all called `f`, two of them with the uniformity
in the *second* argument and one in the first. Re-derive; never copy.

Also in this paper: `ν*(R,ν)` (Lovász's fractional matching supremum),
`C(c)`, `Cap_B(c)`, `L(R,ν)`, `K(r,c)`, `T(B)`. None of them is any `φ`,
`ψ` or `C` used anywhere else in this corpus.
